title: Cum-Clauses
subtitle: cum + subjunctive: when, since, although. The most useful conjunction.
objectives: Recognize circumstantial cum clauses with subjunctive.
Translate as 'when', 'since', or 'although' based on context.
Distinguish temporal cum (with indicative) from circumstantial cum (with subjunctive).

sections.heading: Cum-clauses
sections.body:
cum + subjunctive expresses circumstance:

cum temporal: when
cum causal: since, because
cum concessive: although

Caesar writes: cum Caesar in Galliam pervēnisset, duae factiōnēs erant. — When Caesar had arrived in Gaul, there were two factions.

Cum with indicative = 'when' (simple time). Cum with subjunctive = 'when' (circumstantial), 'since', or 'although'.

items.prompt: Translate: cum hostēs appropinquārent, mīlitēs pugnāvērunt.
items.answer: When the enemies were approaching, the soldiers fought.

items.prompt: Translate: cum Caesar fortis esset, eum timēbant.
items.answer: Since Caesar was brave, they feared him.

words.latin: cum Caesar haec audīvisset, legiōnēs dūxit.
words.gloss: When Caesar had heard these things, he led the legions.
